items.title: fix: Slack DMのスレッド見出しをAgent dispatch前に抑止
items.body:
## 概要

Slack DMでトップレベルの「スレッド見出し」を送信した場合、Hermes Agent自身は作業を開始せず、詳細指示を同じSlackスレッドで受け付ける運用を行っています。しかし現状は `docs/ai/hermes-agent-runtime.md` のruntimeプロンプト指示に依存しており、Slack Adapter / Gateway側にAgent実行前の機械的なガードがありません。

## 現状

- Slack AdapterはトップレベルDMの見出しも通常の `MessageEvent` としてdispatchする
- その結果、セッション作成、Agent実行、LLM/API呼び出し、ツール実行まで進む場合がある
- トップレベルDMでは `source.thread_id` にメッセージtsが合成されるため、`source.thread_id` の有無では実スレッド返信と区別できない
- raw Slack inbound eventの `thread_ts` の有無なら区別できる

## 対応方針

以下をすべて満たすSlackイベントを、Agent dispatch前にSlack Adapterで停止する。

- Slackの1:1 DM (`channel_type=im`)
- raw inbound eventに `thread_ts` が存在しないトップレベルメッセージ
- 設定されたスレッド見出し構文に一致する本文

見出し受信時はLLM / Agentを経由せず、元メッセージへのSlackスレッド返信として、固定確認メッセージを1件だけ送信する。

> 見出しとして受信しました。詳細はこのスレッドに送ってください。

設定可能な接頭辞・確認メッセージとして実装し、この環境では接頭辞 `スレッド` を使用する。実スレッド返信（raw `thread_ts`あり）は、本文が同じ接頭辞で始まっていても通常処理する。

## 完了条件

- runtime文書の意図と実動作が一致する
- セッション作成・Agent取得・LLM/API呼び出し・ツール実行・ファイル処理より前に停止する
- `スレッド`、`スレッド Hermes`、全角空白、読点などの表記揺れを扱う
- `スレッドについて調べて` のような通常文を誤抑止しない
- トップレベルDM、通常DM、実スレッド返信、`thread_ts == ts` 境界ケース、固定応答の重複送信をテストする

items.title: [Bug]: Bot Mode cold-wake / stranded resume with many profiles

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

Bug report for Hermes devs: Bot Mode cold-wake / stranded resume with many profiles

Product: Hermes Desktop + hermes-bots (Bot Mode / multi-profile)
Version: Hermes Agent v0.20.4 (2026.8.18) · local de213b52 (dirty) · Desktop package reports 0.17.0
OS: Linux (XFCE)
Setup: ~10 specialist profiles in one Bot Mode group (“Bullet Journal”), each backed by its own hermes serve child; shared local llama.cpp (--parallel 1)

───

Summary

With Bot Mode and many profiles, idle backend teardown is expected and desirable for RAM. After a backend is reaped/evicted, reopening that bot often fails with:

Couldn't load this session
The connection to this session failed and automatic retries gave up…

Users also see bots hang on “Waking up”, or open the wrong chat (e.g. a cron job transcript) when ui_meta.hermes-bots.chat points at a bad session.

Idle kill is fine. Sticky resume of a dead WebSocket / UI session id after idle kill is the bug. Keeping backends alive for hours is only a workaround and fights the pool’s purpose.

───

Expected behavior

1. Bot idle → Desktop reaps that profile’s hermes serve (save RAM).
2. User clicks the bot → Desktop cold-starts the backend (~1–2s is OK).
3. UI either:
   • rehydrates the canonical forever-chat from state.db, or
   • mints a new forever-chat if the live WS handle is gone.
4. User chats. No stranded error.

Pool should mean: bound concurrent processes, not “resume must succeed against a corpse.”

───

Actual behavior

1. Backend reaped (Reaping idle profile backend "…" (idle > Ns)) or LRU-evicted (Evicting idle … (LRU cap 3)).
2. UI still holds / retries an old session association (session.reclaimed with reason: "ws_orphan_reap").
3. Resume retries exhaust → stranded UI (resumeStrandedTitle in Desktop i18n).
4. Sometimes agent init starts on the profile backend but the UI never gets a clean turn (hang / “Waking up”).
5. Separately: profile.yaml → ui_meta.hermes-bots.chat can be set to a cron_* session, so the bot opens a cron digest instead of a forever-chat.

───

Environment / scale that triggers it

┌─────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Factor                          │ Our case                                                                                                          │
├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Bot Mode group size             │ 10 profiles (AI, Arsenal, Article Writing, Book Writing, Career, Coding, Fitness, Home, Office, Photography)      │
├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Desktop pool defaults (source)  │ HERMES_DESKTOP_POOL_MAX default 3; HERMES_DESKTOP_POOL_IDLE_MS default 10 minutes (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts) │
├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Effect of defaults with 10 bots │ Constant reap + LRU thrash while switching bots / using group chat                                                │
├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Inference                       │ Local OpenAI-compatible llama-server, --parallel 1 (cold wakes can queue and feel hung)                           │
└─────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Defaults that make multi-bot painful:

const POOL_MAX_BACKENDS = Math.max(1, Number(process.env.HERMES_DESKTOP_POOL_MAX) || 3)
const POOL_IDLE_MS = Math.max(60_000, Number(process.env.HERMES_DESKTOP_POOL_IDLE_MS) || 10 * 60_000)

Raising pool max/idle reduces how often you hit the bug; it does not fix cold-wake resume.

───

Repro (reliable enough)

1. Create ≥5–10 Bot Mode profiles in one group (or use an existing multi-bot group).
2. Launch Desktop with defaults (pool max 3, idle 10m) — or raise max but keep a short idle.
3. Open several bots / the group chat so multiple profile backends spawn.
4. Leave one bot untouched until Desktop logs show it reaped, e.g.
   Reaping idle profile backend "career-management" (idle > 600s)
   (or wait for LRU: Evicting idle profile backend "…" (LRU cap 3)).
5. Click that bot again (or return to its forever-chat tab).
6. Observe stranded resume and/or long wake hang; Desktop log shows ws_orphan_reap for the stored session id.

Optional aggravator: pin ui_meta.hermes-bots.chat to a cron_* session id and open the bot — wrong transcript + confusing “off” personality.

───

Log evidence (sanitized)

Idle reap / LRU (defaults):

Reaping idle profile backend "career-management" (idle > 600s)
Evicting idle profile backend "ai" (LRU cap 3)

After raising idle to 1h (still reaps; cold wake still fragile):

Reaping idle profile backend "photography" (idle > 3600s)

Orphan reclaim of UI sessions (including cron ids and normal desktop chats):

{
  "type": "session.reclaimed",
  "payload": {
    "session_id": "1f62f403",
    "stored_session_id": "20260818_175913_6bdff1",
    "reason": "ws_orphan_reap"
  }
}

{
  "type": "session.reclaimed",
  "payload": {
    "session_id": "f0d23207",
    "stored_session_id": "cron_1e36113b135a_20260818_174837",
    "reason": "ws_orphan_reap"
  }
}

User-facing copy (apps/desktop/src/i18n/en.ts):

resumeStrandedTitle: "Couldn't load this session",
resumeStrandedBody:
  'The connection to this session failed and automatic retries gave up. Check that the gateway is running, then try again.',
(Gateway can be healthy; the failure is profile-backend / WS resume, so this message is misleading.)

Wrong canonical chat pin (observed):
Photography ui_meta.hermes-bots.chat = cron_1e36113b135a_20260818_173303 titled “Arsenal Morning Digest” — bot opened a cron run, not a photo forever-chat.

───

Root cause (working theory)

Three interacting issues:

1. Cold start ≠ clean remount
   After pool reap/evict, Desktop treats the old UI/WS session as resumable. When the live handle is gone (ws_orphan_reap), retries end in stranded UI instead of DB rehydrate or remint.

2. Sticky forever-chat pointer
   profile.yaml → ui_meta.hermes-bots.chat survives backend death. If that id is stale, or worse a cron_* session, wake is doomed or wrong.

3. Defaults hostile to Bot Mode at scale
   Cap 3 + 10m idle with ~10 bots guarantees teardown under normal use, amplifying (1)–(2). Group chat that touches many members makes it worse.

Pool eviction accounting itself looks intentional (apps/desktop/electron/pool-eviction.ts); the gap is wake path after teardown.

───

Suggested product fixes (for a future release)

P0 — Wake must tolerate backend death
On open bot / resume forever-chat, if WS resume fails or session was ws_orphan_reap’d:

1. Ensure profile backend is up.
2. Load history from state.db by stored session id, or
3. If not loadable / not a desktop forever-chat → automatically mint a new canonical chat and update ui_meta.hermes-bots.chat.
4. Never leave the user on stranded UI as the steady state after a normal idle reap.

“Retry” should do the same automated recovery, not only re-hit a dead id.

P0 — Never pin cron (or non-desktop) sessions as bot forever-chats
• Reject / ignore chat: values matching cron_* (and ideally source != desktop).
• When a cron run completes under a profile, do not write that session id into hermes-bots.chat.
• Optionally hide/archive cron sessions from the bot’s primary chat entry point.

P1 — Bot Mode–aware pool defaults or presets
For users with many bots:

• Higher default POOL_MAX when Bot Mode / N profiles detected, or
• Documented preset: e.g. POOL_MAX >= bot_count, idle 15–30m.

Important: do not “fix” resume solely by refusing to idle-kill. Idle kill should stay.

P1 — Clearer stranded UX
• If gateway is up but profile backend was cold-starting, say that.
• Offer “Open new chat for this bot” as a one-click recovery that clears the bad pin.

P2 — Group chat wake
Opening a group should not strand member bots whose backends were reaped; members should cold-start in the background without blocking the room on one failed resume.

P2 — Optional: auto-remint policy
Setting: “On resume failure, always remint forever-chat” (default on for Bot Mode). History can still be browsable via session list.

───

Workarounds we used (not ideal long-term)

1. Clear ui_meta.hermes-bots.chat on all group bots so the next open mints fresh (avoids resume of dead/cron ids).
2. Raise HERMES_DESKTOP_POOL_MAX=16 so mid-session LRU thrash stops.
3. Use a moderate idle (HERMES_DESKTOP_POOL_IDLE_MS=1800000 = 30m) — save RAM, accept cold start if wake remints cleanly.
4. Avoid “keep backends 12h” as the real fix (resource nightmare; hides the bug).

Note: hermes desktop sometimes rewrites ~/.local/share/applications/hermes.desktop Exec= and drops the pool env — easy to lose the workaround after a launcher refresh.

───

What we are not asking for

• Disabling the pool or keeping all bot processes resident forever.
• Treating stranded resume as “user error / check gateway” when gateway is fine.

We want backends to turn off when idle. We need cold wake to be a first-class, automatic path for Bot Mode forever-chats.

───

Ask

Please consider:

1. Auto-recover (rehydrate or remint) when forever-chat resume fails after pool reap/evict.
2. Guardrails so hermes-bots.chat cannot point at cron_* / non-desktop sessions.
3. Bot Mode–scaled pool defaults or docs, without making long idle the official solution.

Happy to provide fuller desktop.log slices, profile.yaml samples, or a minimal multi-profile repro if useful.

### Steps to Reproduce

Create multiple bots
Toggle between them after the normal timeout period

### Expected Behavior

Should be able to switch back and forth without issue

### Actual Behavior

Please see above

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell

```

### Operating System

Linux Mint XFCE

items.title: [Bug]: Opening a group chat in Bots section also opens it in the menu, hiding the bot list
items.body:
## Bug Description

Opening a group chat from the **Bots** section of the Hermes desktop app also opens the same chat in the menu/session area by mistake, leaving no visibility of the list of bots.

The Bots section navigation is replaced by the opened group chat: instead of keeping the bot list visible (or showing the chat in place of it), the chat room takes over both the left panel and the main area, and the group chat also appears as an active item in the top menu (alongside SESSIONS / CRONJOBS). To get back to the bot list you have to leave the chat.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the **Bots** section in the Hermes desktop app (bot mode with a group chat that has 2+ bots, e.g. "The Coding Room").
2. Click on the group chat to open it.
3. The chat opens in the Bots section **and** also opens in the menu/sessions area, hiding the list of bots.

## Expected Behavior

Opening a group chat in the Bots section should keep the bot list visible — the chat should open in place of the bot list within the Bots section (or as a dedicated sub-view), and should NOT also open/duplicate in the menu/sessions area.

## Actual Behavior

The group chat opens in the Bots section AND in the menu/sessions area at the same time, leaving no visibility of the list of bots. See attached screenshot (comment below).

## Environment

- App: Hermes Agent desktop
- Section: Bots / group chat (bot mode)
- OS: macOS (OrbStack Linux VM backend)

items.title: Bot Mode group chat room log not persisted across machines (stored in localStorage)
items.body:
## Description

When using Hermes Desktop connected to a remote backend (via `hermes serve`), the Bot Mode group chat conversation history does not persist across machines. The group chat appears empty on a second machine even though both machines are connected to the same remote backend.

Individual bot 1:1 sessions work correctly across machines — only the group chat view is affected.

## Root Cause

The group chat room log (the shared conversation view that coordinates round-robin bot responses) is stored in the Desktop app's local plugin storage (`ctx.storage`), which resolves to `window.localStorage` — completely machine-local with no server-side sync.

The storage chain:

```
ctx.storage.set('group-chats', durable)
  -> createPluginStorage(pluginId).set(key, value)
    -> writeKey(`hermes.plugin.hermes-bots.group-chats`, JSON.stringify(value))
      -> window.localStorage.setItem(...)
```

Source: `apps/desktop/src/lib/storage.ts` — `readKey`/`writeKey` use `window.localStorage`.

Meanwhile, individual bot sessions are stored in each profile's `state.db` on the OCI backend, which IS accessed remotely. Bot meta (avatars, titles) also syncs via `profiles.configure` + `ui_meta`. Only the group chat room log lacks a server-side persistence path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up Hermes Desktop on Machine A connected to a remote backend via `hermes serve`
2. Create a group chat with multiple bots and have a conversation
3. Set up Hermes Desktop on Machine B connected to the same remote backend
4. Open the group chat on Machine B — it shows empty ("No messages yet — say hi...")

## Expected Behavior

The group chat conversation history should be accessible across machines when both are connected to the same remote backend, since the conversation data already exists on the server in each bot profile's `state.db`.

## Actual Behavior

The group chat room is empty on Machine B. Individual bot sessions still show their message history.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop v0.20.4
- Backend: remote `hermes serve` on Linux (ARM64)
- Machines: macOS and Linux (both connecting to the same remote backend)
- Both machines connected to the backend via Tailscale

## Suggested Fix

Persist the group chat room log server-side (e.g., in the gateway's session store or via a `ui_meta`-style mechanism) so it follows the user across machines. The room log data (`log`, `watermarks`, `members`, `sessions`) could be serialized and stored alongside the bot meta that already syncs.

items.title: [Feature]: Persist Bot Mode group chat room log server-side for cross-machine sync
items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

When using Hermes Desktop connected to a remote backend (`hermes serve`), the Bot Mode group chat conversation history does not persist across machines. The group chat appears empty on a second machine even though both machines are connected to the same remote backend.

Individual bot 1:1 sessions work correctly across machines — only the unified group chat view is affected. This is because:

- **Individual bot sessions** are stored in each profile's `state.db` on the server, accessed remotely ✅
- **Bot meta** (avatars, titles) syncs via `profiles.configure` + `ui_meta` ✅
- **Group chat room log** (the shared conversation view) is stored in `window.localStorage` via the plugin's `ctx.storage` — completely machine-local ❌

The storage chain:

```
ctx.storage.set('group-chats', durable)
  → createPluginStorage(pluginId).set(key, value)
    → writeKey(`hermes.plugin.hermes-bots.group-chats`, JSON.stringify(value))
      → window.localStorage.setItem(...)
```

Source: `apps/desktop/src/lib/storage.ts` — `readKey`/`writeKey` use `window.localStorage`.

This means users with a multi-machine setup (e.g. desktop + laptop, both connecting to the same remote backend) cannot see their group chat history when switching devices, even though all the individual conversation data already exists server-side.

## Proposed Solution

Persist the group chat room log server-side so it follows the user across machines. The room log data (`log`, `watermarks`, `members`, `sessions`) could be stored via the same `ui_meta` mechanism that already syncs bot meta, or in the gateway's session store alongside the individual bot sessions.

The group **membership** list already syncs cross-machine (via `profile.yaml ui_meta`) — only the conversation log needs a server-side persistence path.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Local-only (status quo):** Works for single-machine users but breaks the experience for remote-backend users with multiple devices.
- **Reconstruct from individual bot sessions:** The conversation data exists in each bot's `state.db` on the server, but reconstructing the unified group view from per-bot sessions would be complex and lose the coordination state (watermarks, thread tracking).

## Feature Type

Gateway / messaging improvement

## Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines) — the room log serialization already exists (`durableGroupChatMembers` and the `ctx.storage.set('group-chats', ...)` path); the main work is adding a server-side storage backend and hydration on plugin load.

items.title: bug(bot-mode): 'Create on' picker never appears — plugin expects array, IPC returns registry object
items.body:
## Summary

The Bot Mode **"Create on"** picker never appears in the New Agent dialog, even with multiple connections registered — the plugin expects an array from `host.connections()` but the IPC handler returns the registry **object**, so the gate `connections.length > 1` never fires and the dialog silently degrades to single-connection behavior.

Docs promise the picker: [bot-mode.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/website/docs/user-guide/bot-mode.md) — *"With more than one connection registered in Settings → Connections, the New Agent dialog grows a **Create on** picker."*

## Root cause

**Plugin** (`apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js`):

```js
host
  .connections()
  .then(value => setConnections(Array.isArray(value) ? value : []))
  .catch(() => setConnections([]))
```

Gate (same file, New Agent dialog):

```js
Array.isArray(connections) && connections.length > 1
  ? labeled('Create on', ...)
  : null
```

**SDK** (`apps/desktop/src/sdk/index.ts`) — `connections()` resolves `window.hermesDesktop.connections.list()`, which is the IPC handler `hermes:connections:list` (`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`):

```js
ipcMain.handle('hermes:connections:list', async () => sanitizeConnectionsRegistry())
```

`sanitizeConnectionsRegistry()` returns an **object** — not an array:

```js
{
  version, primary, launchMode, lastUsed, secureTokenStorage,
  connections: [ ...sanitized entries... ]
}
```

So `Array.isArray(value)` is always `false` → `connections` is always `[]` → the picker is hidden regardless of how many connections are registered.

## Expected behavior

With ≥ 2 connections (e.g. local + remote gateway), the New Agent dialog shows the **Create on** picker so a bot can be created on another machine's backend, per the docs and the `host.connections()` SDK contract ("The registered connection list").

## Suggested fix

Unwrap the registry object in the plugin, matching how the Gateways settings page consumes it:

```js
host
  .connections()
  .then(v => setConnections(Array.isArray(v?.connections) ? v.connections : []))
  .catch(() => setConnections([]))
```

(or change the IPC handler to return a bare array — the SDK docstring says "The registered connection list", so returning `sanitizeConnectionsRegistry().connections` may be the cleaner contract).

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop v0.20.4 (packaged release, clean tree) + `hermes-agent` main @ 4903993cdd
- `connections.json` (registry v2) contains 2 connections: `local` ("This device") + one remote gateway
- Reproduced on Windows; logic is platform-independent

## Related

- Docs fix for the local "This device" connect-on-demand roster behavior: #89790
- This bug is why cross-machine bot creation via the picker is currently impossible despite the multi-connection feature being documented.

items.title: [Bug]: Bot Mode — opening a group chat lands in the middle of the room, not on the last message
items.body:
## Bug Description

Clicking a Bot Mode **group chat** does not land on the latest message. The room opens scrolled to the middle of the discussion (start of the currently expanded thread), not the bottom.

1:1 Bot Chats use the normal session transcript, which has sticky-bottom behavior. The group room is a custom `ScrollArea` over `$groupChats[group].log` with **no scroll-to-bottom on open**.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop → **Bots**.
2. Open a group that already has several messages / more than one thread.
3. Leave the room (or switch away) and click the same group again.

## Expected Behavior

Opening a group chat should show the latest activity: viewport pinned to the bottom of the room log (newest thread + last line), same as opening a 1:1 chat.

## Actual Behavior

The log mounts at `scrollTop = 0`. Older threads are collapsed to summary rows; the newest thread is expanded from its **first** message (`expanded = openThreads[id] ?? isNewest`). That first expanded message sits in the middle of the overall history, which is where the user lands.

## Source

`apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js` — `GroupChatWorkspace`

- Log is rendered oldest → newest inside a Radix `ScrollArea` (`className: 'min-h-0 flex-1'`).
- No `useEffect` / end sentinel / `scrollTop = scrollHeight` on mount or when `group` changes.
- Thread fold: newest thread open from the head, older threads collapsed. Combined with scroll-at-top, this reads as \"I opened the room in the middle of the discussion.\"

## Environment

- App: Hermes Agent desktop
- Feature: Bot Mode group chat room (plugin workspace, not a stored session transcript)

## Related, not duplicates

- #84997 — switching into a streaming **session** lands on old history (core transcript, not the group room log)
- #78486 — chat view jumps to a historical block while the assistant is still responding
- #70618 — session viewport does not auto-scroll after task completion
- #89788 — opening a group also opens it in the menu
- #89800 — persist the group room log server-side

items.body:
# [Bug] muse-spark-1.2 via opencode-go /v1/responses returns EmptyStream (HTTP 200 SSE, no finish_reason) — retried 3x, 73s delay

**Related:** NousResearch/hermes-agent#65631

## Summary
After switching to `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.2` (endpoint `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses`, SDK `@ai-sdk/openai` per https://opencode.ai/docs/zh-cn/go/ 2026-08-18), a simple `你好` prompt triggers `EmptyStreamError` and 3 stream retries with `tcp_force_closed=1`, totaling ~73s before the final 212-char response is delivered.

Suspect: upstream returns HTTP 200 SSE with an empty chunk (choices=None / no finish_reason), which Hermes' chat/responses streaming path drops and then hits the zero-chunk guard:
```
if finish_reason is None and not content_parts and not reasoning_parts and not tool_calls_acc:
    raise EmptyStreamError("Provider returned an empty stream with no finish_reason ...")
```

## Reproduction
1. `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` valid (tier Go $10/mo). Model list `GET /v1/models` confirms `muse-spark-1.2` and `muse-spark-1.2-contributor` exist.
2. Hermes patched: `opencode_model_api_mode` now maps `muse-` → `codex_responses` (verified: `resolve_runtime_provider(requested='opencode-go', target_model='muse-spark-1.2')` → `api_mode: codex_responses`, `base_url: https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`).
3. Command: `/model muse-spark-1.2 --provider opencode-go` → switch succeeds (`api_mode: codex_responses`).
4. Send `你好`.

Direct API control (same key, same endpoint): `POST /v1/responses {"model":"muse-spark-1.2","input":"Reply with exactly: OK-42","max_output_tokens":50}` → `status: incomplete, reason: max_output_tokens, reasoning_tokens: 47` (reasoning exhausted budget). With `reasoning.effort: low, max_output_tokens: 500` → `status: completed, output: OK-42`. So model itself works when given enough budget.

## Timeline (desensitized, JST+08)

```
14:43:52 inbound msg='你好' (model=muse-spark-1.2 provider=opencode-go)
14:43:54 OpenAI client created (chat_completion_stream_request)
14:44:31 stream_retry_cleanup tcp_force_closed=1 (attempt 1)
14:44:39 stream_retry_cleanup tcp_force_closed=1 (attempt 2)
14:44:47 stream_error_cleanup tcp_force_closed=1
14:44:47 EmptyStreamError: Provider returned an empty stream with no finish_reason (possible upstream error or malformed SSE response). [attempt 1/3]
14:44:47 Retrying in 2.43s (policy=default)
14:44:50 client created (retry)
14:44:56 stream_retry_cleanup tcp_force_closed=1
```

## Bug Description

The Bot Mode **group** composer (new-thread box and reply-in-thread box) has two input bugs:

1. **No newline.** Enter sends. There is no Shift+Enter (or any) line break. The field is a single-line \`<input>\`, not a textarea, so a newline cannot exist even by paste in a useful way.
2. **@ autocomplete is not usable.** #89049 added \`GroupMentionInput\` (merged in #89082). Typing \`@\` still does not present a usable member list in the group workspace tile. \`@everyone\` / \`@all\` are implemented in the parser and in the popover *data*, but the user never sees them.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a Bot Mode group chat (main workspace tile).
2. In the bottom composer, press Enter mid-sentence → the message sends. Press Shift+Enter → still no line break.
3. Type \`@\` or \`@a\` → no visible member / @everyone / @all list.

## Expected Behavior

- Shift+Enter (or the same convention as the main composer) inserts a newline. Enter still sends when the mention popover is closed.
- Typing \`@\` shows seated members plus \`@everyone\` and \`@all\`. Choosing one inserts the string \`parseGroupChatMentions\` already resolves.

## Actual Behavior

Single-line \`Input\`. Form submit on Enter. Mention popover is coded but not reachable in practice.

## Source

\`apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js\`

- Composer is \`GroupMentionInput\` wrapping the SDK \`Input\` (\`<input>\`, not textarea).
- Popover is \`absolute bottom-full\` inside a \`relative\` wrapper at the **bottom** of the room.
- The plugin workspace surface is \`overflow-hidden\` (\`apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/surfaces.tsx\`). A popover that opens upward from the bottom composer is clipped — it looks like \"no autocomplete\".
- \`parseGroupChatMentions\` already treats \`@everyone\` and \`@all\` as the same everyone-flag. No new alias is needed; the gap is discoverability.

## Why this is not #52952 or #89049

- #52952 is the **main session** composer (Enter sends, wants a setting). The group room is a different widget and cannot newline at all.
- #89049 is closed: the popover was added. This report is that the popover still does not show in the workspace tile (clip / surface), so the advertised \`@name\` / \`@everyone\` / \`@all\` path remains unreachable.

## Environment

- App: Hermes Desktop, Bot Mode group room

- #89049 (closed) / #89082 — popover added

items.title: [Bug]: Codex tool follow-ups can send unsupported prompt_cache_retention to gpt-5.6-sol

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-caching
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break/degrade prompt caching or cache-key stability (invariant)

items.body:
## Bug description

The ChatGPT OAuth Codex backend intermittently rejects second/later Responses requests for `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol` with:

```text
HTTP 400: prompt_cache_retention is not supported on this model
```

The model itself is available: the first request succeeds, a Hermes tool executes, and the follow-up model request then fails. Hermes classifies the 400 as non-retryable and aborts the turn.

This was observed repeatedly through the Discord gateway on 2026-08-19. It is distinct from #81558, where the backend rejected the model itself, and from #72351, which concerns an unsupported `temperature` value in title generation.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the ChatGPT OAuth Codex provider:

   ```yaml
   model:
     provider: openai-codex
     default: gpt-5.6-sol
     base_url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex
   ```

2. Start the gateway and send a task that requires at least one tool call.
3. Observe that API call #1 can succeed and the tool can complete.
4. On affected turns, the next Responses request fails with the 400 above.

The failure is intermittent rather than occurring on every tool follow-up.

## Expected behavior

Hermes must not send `prompt_cache_retention` to the consumer ChatGPT Codex endpoint when the selected model does not support it. Tool follow-up requests should complete normally.

## Actual behavior

Sanitized log excerpt from one occurrence:

```text
API call #1: model=gpt-5.6-sol provider=openai-codex ...
tool skill_view completed
API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=BadRequestError
provider=openai-codex base_url=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex
model=gpt-5.6-sol
summary=HTTP 400: prompt_cache_retention is not supported on this model
Non-retryable client error: ... param='prompt_cache_retention' code='invalid_parameter'
```

This occurred multiple times across fresh and existing gateway sessions. No secrets or message contents are included here.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.4 (2026.8.18), git install
- Reproduced from commit `2163f7f8ca82f7c892c7e815dadd80a1486cc194`
- Checked current upstream `main` at `9c6ecf2ca72aa2771ea9abfe682a5986e00a1a6b`; it still has no final Codex wire-boundary guard
- Fedora Linux 43
- Python 3.11.16
- OpenAI SDK 2.24.0
- Provider: `openai-codex`
- Model: `gpt-5.6-sol`
- Gateway platform: Discord

## Root-cause analysis

The normal transport builder appears correct:

- `agent.transports.codex._default_prompt_cache_retention_for_request("gpt-5.6-sol", "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex")` returns `None`.
- An isolated `AIAgent._build_api_kwargs()` probe for the same provider/model/base URL contains no `prompt_cache_retention`.

However, `agent/codex_runtime.py::run_codex_stream()` sends the request at this final boundary:

```python
def _open_codex_stream(next_api_kwargs):
    stream_kwargs = dict(next_api_kwargs)
    stream_kwargs["stream"] = True
    return active_client.responses.create(**stream_kwargs)
```

`next_api_kwargs` is supplied after the Relay/request-middleware path. There is no endpoint-capability sanitization after that final transformation. The exact upstream mutation remains intermittent, but a late-added retention field reaches the SDK unchanged and reproduces the provider's observed 400.

## Proposed fix

Defensively sanitize at the final wire boundary, after Relay/middleware transformation:

```python
stream_kwargs = dict(next_api_kwargs)
if agent._is_codex_backend():
    stream_kwargs.pop("prompt_cache_retention", None)
stream_kwargs["stream"] = True
```

Scope the guard specifically to the consumer ChatGPT OAuth Codex backend so compatible endpoints such as Meta Model API and Bedrock Mantle retain their supported `24h` behavior.

## Local validation

A local patch implementing that guard was exercised as follows:

- RED regression test injected `prompt_cache_retention: "24h"` at the final `run_codex_stream` boundary and confirmed it reached `responses.create()` before the fix.
- GREEN after the guard: the field was absent at `responses.create()`.
- Compatibility test confirmed non-consumer endpoints keep the retention field.
- Relevant suites: **143 passed, 0 failed**.
- Real `gpt-5.6-sol` tool-loop probe: API call #1 succeeded, terminal tool executed, API call #2 succeeded, final result `PROBE_OK`.
- Gateway restarted onto the patch and reconnected to Discord successfully.

The local patch is not yet submitted as a PR.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop status bar right-click always shows the fallback menu — "Show in status bar" (and the context meter) unreachable
items.body:
## Summary

Right-clicking the desktop status bar **always** shows the window-verbs fallback menu (New session / New window / Command palette / **Toggle status bar** / Settings / Update Hermes). The status bar's own context menu — the one with the **"Show in status bar"** item list (Context meter, Turn timer, Session timer, Terminal, Approvals, Gateway, Workspace, …) — is unreachable. As a result the context-usage meter (hidden by default) **cannot be enabled from the UI at all**, and the same is true for every other default-hidden status bar item.

This is a regression introduced by the app-wide context menu coordinator refactor; it is present on `main` (verified at `13ce0c5c`, the current HEAD as of 2026-08-19).

**Platform:** Windows (Hermes Desktop, remote-gateway mode) · also affects macOS/Linux (pure renderer code)

## Root cause

`apps/desktop/src/app/context-menu/app-context-menu.tsx` (from `1314a539c2`, "refactor(desktop): custom translated context menus across the app") installs a capture-phase `contextmenu` listener on `window` and bails out for surfaces that own a Radix context menu:

```ts
// app-context-menu.tsx (~line 612, at 13ce0c5c)
if (element?.closest('[data-slot="context-menu-trigger"]')) {
  return
}
```

The status bar's menu *is* a Radix `ContextMenuTrigger`, wrapped by the shared UI primitive:

```tsx
// components/ui/context-menu.tsx
function ContextMenuTrigger({ ...props }) {
  return <ContextMenuPrimitive.Trigger data-slot="context-menu-trigger" {...props} />
}
```

but the status bar renders it with `asChild` over its own `<footer>`:

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/app/shell/statusbar-controls.tsx (~line 101)
<ContextMenuTrigger asChild>
  <footer
    className={...}
    data-slot="statusbar"   // <-- overwrites the trigger's data-slot
    {...props}
  >
```

Radix `Slot` merges `mergeProps(slotProps, childProps)` — the **child's props win** — so the rendered footer ends up with `data-slot="statusbar"` and *no* `data-slot="context-menu-trigger"`. The coordinator's guard therefore never matches, the listener calls `stopPropagation()`, and the footer's own Radix menu never gets the gesture. The user always gets the fallback menu instead.

Any `ContextMenuTrigger` whose `asChild` child sets its own `data-slot` is affected the same way; the status bar is the one that ships broken.

## Reproduction

1. Install/update Hermes Desktop to a build ≥ `1314a539c2` (current `main`).
2. Ensure the status bar is visible (`Ctrl+Shift+S` toggles it).
3. Right-click anywhere on the status bar strip (bottom of the window).
4. **Actual:** the generic window-verbs menu appears (ends in "Toggle status bar").
5. **Expected:** the status bar's own menu — header "Show in status bar" + per-item checkboxes + "Reset to defaults" + "Hide status bar".

Consequence: with `context-usage` in `STATUSBAR_HIDDEN_BY_DEFAULT` (`statusbar-prefs.ts`), there is no UI path to enable the context meter on an affected build.

## Suggested fixes

**A. Minimal (one line, in the coordinator guard):**

```ts
if (element?.closest('[data-slot="context-menu-trigger"], [data-slot="statusbar"]')) {
  return
}
```

**B. Root-cause (preferred):** stop relying on the overloaded `data-slot` for coordinator detection. The shared `ContextMenuTrigger` wrapper already stamps every trigger with a unique attribute; give it a dedicated, non-colliding one and guard on that instead:

```tsx
// components/ui/context-menu.tsx
return <ContextMenuPrimitive.Trigger
  data-slot="context-menu-trigger"
  data-hermes-context-menu-trigger=""
  {...props}
/>
```

```ts
// app-context-menu.tsx
if (element?.closest('[data-hermes-context-menu-trigger]')) {
  return
}
```

A child can still clobber `data-slot`, but it will not clobber the detection attribute (and the `data-slot` overwrite is already happening today).

## Local verification / workaround

A one-line bundle patch (fix A) was applied directly to the built bundle on a
local Windows build
(`win-unpacked/resources/app.asar.unpacked/dist/assets/index-*.js`):

```js
// before
if (t?.closest(`[data-slot="context-menu-trigger"]`)) return;
// after
if (t?.closest(`[data-slot="context-menu-trigger"],[data-slot="statusbar"]`)) return;
```

**This does not work as a user-facing workaround on Windows.** The app then
failed to start (fully white splash) with:

```
[renderer console:main] Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input
(file:///C:/.../resources/app.asar/dist/assets/index-*.js:421)
```

The patched file on disk was intact and full-size, but its SHA256 no longer
matched the integrity hash embedded in the `app.asar` header, so the asar
integrity check truncated the read and V8 parsed a partial file. Restoring the
original file brought the app back. See the addendum comment for details.

**Conclusion:** there is currently no in-place workaround — the fix must ship
via a rebuild/release (source-level fix A or B above), or the asar must be
repacked with a recomputed integrity header. The source-level change itself is
small (one selector in the coordinator guard, or the dedicated-attribute
approach) and low-risk.

## Related

- #89355 — same coordinator, different symptom: chat-link right-clicks fall through to the app menu instead of the link menu.
- #80341 — status bar / context-usage hidden by default with no discoverable entry point; on builds ≥ `1314a539c2` the missing entry point *is* this bug.
- #78220 — earlier report of the status bar hidden by default after an update (superseded default in current code; `context-usage` is still default-hidden).

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop, Electron build from `main` @ `13ce0c5c67` (2026-08-19)
- Windows 10/11, remote-gateway connection mode

items.title: [Bug]: Bot Mode recreating a same-name group reuses old member sessions

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug description

Recreating a Bot Mode group chat with the same display name can resume the previous per-member group sessions instead of creating a fresh room context. This is especially easy to trigger with the auto-generated group name when it is already at the 64-character limit.

The visible result is that newly updated profile instructions/system prompts are not used in the recreated group. Renaming the group to a shorter, unique name creates fresh sessions and the new profile behavior appears correctly.

Tested with Hermes Agent v0.20.4 (2026.8.18) on macOS arm64 Desktop.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Bot Mode group with multiple profiles and use the auto-generated group name.
2. Send a message so each member gets a persistent `Group: <name>` session.
3. Update one or more profile instructions.
4. Disband/delete the group.
5. Create another group with the same members and leave the auto-generated name unchanged.
6. Send a message in the new group.

## Expected behavior

A newly created group is a new room identity. Each member should receive a new per-group session and the system prompt current at room creation should be used.

## Actual behavior

The new group resumes the old `Group: <name>` sessions. Old system prompts and prior session identity are retained. Changing the group display name to a new short value is an effective workaround.

## Root-cause evidence

The Desktop Bots plugin currently treats the group display name as both the room key and the member-session title (`Group: ${group}`). Session creation/resume falls back by that title.

The duplicate-name path also appends ` 2`, ` 3`, etc. and then slices the whole result to 64 characters. If the base name is already 64 characters, slicing removes the suffix, so the supposedly unique name is unchanged and the old room/session title is reused.

## Suggested fix

- Give every newly created group an immutable persisted `roomId` separate from its editable display name.
- Include that `roomId` in per-member session identity/title and use it for resume lookup.
- Preserve `roomId` on rename, but mint a new one after disband/recreate even when the display name is identical.
- For display-name deduplication, reserve suffix length before truncating the base.
- Keep a compatibility fallback for legacy persisted groups that do not yet have a `roomId`.

Useful regression cases:

- Two auto-generated names whose base is exactly 64 characters remain distinct.
- Disbanding and recreating the same display name does not resume old member sessions.
- Renaming an existing room preserves its sessions.
- Legacy groups without `roomId` still hydrate.

## Debug report

Not attached because the issue is reproducible from deterministic Desktop state/session identity behavior and a shared debug upload could include unrelated local profile information.

items.title: `acp` entrypoint ignores process-env credentials that the gateway path honors (spawn-injected `key_env` values never reach the provider call)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
**Version:** Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), Linux.

## Summary

A supervisor that spawns `hermes acp` and injects a provider
credential via the child's environment (the variable named by a
provider block's `key_env`) finds the credential is never used:
turns authenticate with a different credential and fail, while
the same env-var mechanism works for the gateway process. (Later
diagnosis — 2026-08-18, see issue 2 below — identified the
"different credential": the client silently falls back to
`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` when the custom provider's key resolves
empty, and sends it to the custom `base_url`.) The `acp`
path appears to discard process-env credentials that other
entrypoints honor — an inconsistency rather than (I think) an
intended restriction.

## Reproduction

1. A provider block in `config.yaml` with
   `key_env: MY_PROVIDER_KEY` (no literal `api_key`).
2. Remove `MY_PROVIDER_KEY` from `~/.hermes/.env` so the process
   environment is the only source.
3. Spawn `hermes acp` with `MY_PROVIDER_KEY=<valid key>` in the
   child env; drive one turn over ACP (`session/new` +
   `session/prompt`).
4. The upstream provider receives an invalid/placeholder credential
   and returns 401; with a fallback provider configured, the turn
   silently succeeds there instead.

Verified during diagnosis:

- The spawned process's `/proc/<pid>/environ` contains the exact,
  independently-verified-valid key (byte-compared; the same string
  authenticates when presented directly to the provider).
- The same env-var delivery works for the gateway (via a systemd
  drop-in `Environment=` line): gateway turns authenticate fine.
- Ruled out on our side: dotenv override (`load_hermes_dotenv` —
  the key is absent from every `.env`, so nothing overwrites it),
  external secret sources (disabled), and
  `_clear_known_keys_missing_from_dotenv` (scoped to routing keys,
  credentials excluded).

## Suspected mechanism

`agent/secret_scope.get_secret` resolution order: when a secret
scope is installed and multiplexing is active (multiple profiles
configured), the scope is authoritative — a miss returns `default`
and deliberately does not fall through to `os.environ`, because in
a multiplexer the process env may hold another profile's value.
That isolation argument is sound for a multi-profile gateway — but
an `acp`-spawned process serves exactly one session for exactly one
profile, so its own process env cannot leak anything cross-profile.

## Ask

Either of these would resolve it; the first seems cleanest:

1. **In the `acp` entrypoint, seed the session's secret scope from
   the process environment at startup** (or equivalently, let scope
   misses fall through to `os.environ` when the process is a
   single-session `acp` server). The single-session invariant makes
   this safe by construction.
2. A general opt-in, e.g. `HERMES_SCOPE_SEED_KEYS=<comma list>`:
   names listed there are copied from the process env into every
   installed secret scope. Callers explicitly accept the sharing.

Motivation: per-spawn credentials are how a supervisor (in our case
a dashboard that spawns one `hermes acp` per chat session) can give
each session its own virtual key on a LiteLLM-style proxy — enabling
per-session usage/cost attribution with no Hermes configuration
changes at all. Everything works today except this last step.

items.title: [Bug]: pytest tests/hermes_cli/ runs git checkout/merge/stash against the developer's real checkout

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
### Bug Description

Running `pytest tests/hermes_cli/` mutates the checkout you are running it from. It executes real `git checkout main`, `git merge origin/main`, `git stash push --include-untracked` and `git reset --hard HEAD` against the working tree, so **uncommitted work is stashed away and the branch can be switched** mid-run.

I lost an uncommitted edit to it before tracing it. On my machine it produced these, silently:

```
stash@{0}: On main: hermes-update-autostash-20260819-153749
stash@{1}: On main: hermes-update-autostash-20260819-070451
```

and this in the reflog of the repo under test:

```
checkout: moving from 56e0e77d4e to main
merge origin/main: Fast-forward
reset: moving to HEAD
```

Nothing is destroyed (the stash is recoverable) but work silently disappears from the tree, and a checkout on a feature branch can come back on `main`.

`tests/conftest.py` already has a live-system guard written for exactly this hazard — its comment says *"These commands run `git fetch origin + git pull` against the REAL checkout"*. It only inspects argv for `hermes update`, so it catches the **spawned** CLI. It does not catch the **in-process** call, which issues bare `git` commands whose argv contains no "update" at all.

### Steps to Reproduce

Two files, under two seconds, on a clean checkout:

```bash
echo marker > MARKER.txt
pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_skills_subparser.py \
       tests/hermes_cli/test_update_orphan_backend_reap.py -q

git stash list   # hermes-update-autostash-<timestamp>
ls MARKER.txt    # gone
```

Order matters. Neither file does this alone, and `-k update` does not reproduce it because that deselects `test_skills_subparser.py`.

### Root Cause

1. `test_skills_subparser.py` does `del sys.modules['hermes_cli.main']` and re-imports, and never restores it. That installs a **second** `hermes_cli.main` module object for the rest of the session.
2. `test_update_orphan_backend_reap.py` bound `from hermes_cli import main as cli_main` at import time, so it still holds the **first** object.
3. Its `patch.object(cli_main, "PROJECT_ROOT", _RootSentinel())` therefore patches an orphan.
4. `update_cmd._m()` re-imports and gets the **live** module, whose `PROJECT_ROOT` is the real path.
5. The `_RootSentinel` tripwire never fires, and `_cmd_update_impl` proceeds against the real repo.

Captured stack at the moment git ran — note `cwd` is a real `PosixPath`, not the sentinel:

```
test_update_orphan_backend_reap.py:279  cli_main._cmd_update_impl(_update_args(), gateway_mode=False)
hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:4972           _stash_local_changes_if_needed(git_cmd, _m().PROJECT_ROOT)
hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:1487           subprocess.run(cwd=PosixPath('/…/<repo>'))
```

Worth noting the `_RootSentinel` guard is weak independently of this: it only raises on `__truediv__`, and the first thing `_cmd_update_impl` does with the root is hand it to `_discard_lockfile_churn`, which passes it as `subprocess.run(cwd=...)` inside a blanket `try/except` — so when the patch *is* working, the resulting `TypeError` is swallowed rather than tripping the guard.

### Suggested Fix

Two parts, both small:

**1. Restore both bindings in `test_skills_subparser.py`.** `from hermes_cli import main` resolves through the package attribute, which the re-import rebinds as well, so restoring `sys.modules` alone is not sufficient:

```python
def test_no_duplicate_skills_subparser(monkeypatch):
    import hermes_cli
    cached_main = sys.modules.get('hermes_cli.main')
    if cached_main is not None:
        monkeypatch.setattr(hermes_cli, 'main', cached_main, raising=False)
    monkeypatch.delitem(sys.modules, 'hermes_cli.main', raising=False)
```

**2. Extend the existing live-system guard** to block mutating git (`stash`, `checkout`, `merge`, `pull`, `reset`, `clean`, …) whose `cwd` resolves to `PROJECT_ROOT`, threading `kwargs.get("cwd")` into `_check_subprocess_cmd` from both the `_wrap_subprocess` and `_GuardedPopen` paths. Read-only git is left alone so tests can still probe repo state. This turns silent working-tree mutation into an immediate, explanatory test failure, and covers the whole class rather than this one instance.

With both applied the reproducer passes (17 passed) and leaves the tree untouched. Across the full `tests/hermes_cli/` run the totals are essentially unchanged (246 failed / 5957 passed vs 245 / 5958 before, same 9 errors and 81 skips) — and the run no longer mutates the checkout, which the "before" run did, so the baseline itself was measured on a tree being rewritten underneath it.

### One related test worth a look

`test_update_stale_dashboard.py::TestBackCompatAlias::test_alias_is_the_kill_function` passes alone and passes with its own file (35 passed), but fails in a full run once `sys.modules` is restored properly. It asserts identity between two functions rebound from `sys.modules["hermes_cli.main"]`, so it is sensitive to *which* `hermes_cli.main` object is live — it appears to have been relying on the leaked second module. Same fragility class rather than a separate bug, but it needs a look alongside the fix.

I'm happy to open a PR if useful.

items.title: WhatsApp: replying to the bot's own message never triggers a response (JID device-suffix mismatch)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

On WhatsApp with `require_mention: true`, **replying to one of the bot's own messages never triggers a response**. `_message_is_reply_to_bot()` cannot return `True` for any user, because the two identifiers it compares are normalized into shapes that can never be equal.

The same defect silently disables `_message_mentions_bot()`, so a genuine WhatsApp @-mention of the bot is also ignored — group replies only work at all because `mention_patterns` (plain text matching) happens to catch them.

## Root cause

WhatsApp JIDs are `user[:device]@server`. The bridge normalizer replaces the colon with an `@` instead of dropping the device part:

```js
// scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge_helpers.js
export function normalizeWhatsAppId(value) {
  if (!value) return '';
  return String(value).replace(':', '@');
}
```

`botIds` is built from `sock.user.id` / `sock.user.lid`, which carry a device suffix:

```
972500000000:12@s.whatsapp.net  ->  972500000000@12@s.whatsapp.net
```

`quotedParticipant` comes from `contextInfo.participant`, which does **not**:

```
972500000000@s.whatsapp.net     ->  972500000000@s.whatsapp.net
```

So this comparison is always `False`:

```python
# gateway/platforms/whatsapp_common.py
def _message_is_reply_to_bot(self, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    quoted_participant = self._normalize_whatsapp_id(data.get("quotedParticipant"))
    if not quoted_participant:
        return False
    return quoted_participant in self._bot_ids_from_message(data)
```

`_normalize_whatsapp_id()` on the Python side only does `":" -> "@"` again, so it does not reconcile the two forms either.

## Steps to reproduce

1. WhatsApp platform, `mode: bot`, in a group, with `require_mention: true`
2. Have the bot post a message
3. Quote-reply to that message **without** typing anything matching `mention_patterns`
4. Nothing happens — no response, and no log line anywhere, because the gate is silent

Typing a mention pattern works, which is what masks the bug.

## Proposed fix

Compare on the device-stripped form. This collapses any number of `@`-separated segments to `first@last`, so it is correct both for `user:device@server` and for the already-mangled `user@device@server` the current normalizer produces:

```python
@staticmethod
def _bare_jid(value: str) -> str:
    """WhatsApp JIDs are user[:device]@server. Our own id carries a device suffix and a quoted
    participant does not, so the raw forms never compare equal."""
    s = str(value or "").strip()
    if "@" not in s:
        return s
    parts = s.split("@")
    return parts[0] + "@" + parts[-1]

def _message_is_reply_to_bot(self, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    quoted_participant = self._bare_jid(self._normalize_whatsapp_id(data.get("quotedParticipant")))
    if not quoted_participant:
        return False
    bot_ids = {self._bare_jid(b) for b in self._bot_ids_from_message(data)}
    return quoted_participant in bot_ids
```

And the same treatment in `_message_mentions_bot()`, immediately before the intersection:

```python
bot_ids = {self._bare_jid(b) for b in bot_ids}
mentioned_ids = {self._bare_jid(m) for m in mentioned_ids}
if mentioned_ids & bot_ids:
```

Fixing `normalizeWhatsAppId` in the bridge to strip the device instead of rewriting the colon would also work and is arguably the more correct place, but it changes an identifier shape used elsewhere (allowlists, `mentionedIds`, `readReceiptKey`), so the narrower fix above is the safer one to start from.

## Verification

Applied against v0.20.4 on a live deployment. Before: every quoted reply to the bot was ignored. After: three consecutive quoted replies were answered with no mention text typed, and an instrumented counter for "quoted reply judged not-to-bot" fired **zero** times over the same period.

That the fix is exactly "drop the middle segments" is itself the evidence for the diagnosis — those middle segments only exist when `replace(':', '@')` has fired on a device suffix.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.4 (2026.8.18)
- WhatsApp (Baileys bridge), `mode: bot`, group with `group_policy: allowlist`, `require_mention: true`
- Confirmed still present on `main` at the time of writing (`bridge_helpers.js`, `whatsapp_common.py`)

items.title: [Feature]: Restore per-profile remote override UI — switch a remote agent (WSL/cloud/multi-machine) like a local profile
items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

I run several Hermes agents (one local on Windows, one in WSL, and I plan more on other machines/cloud). I want to manage them all from **one desktop app instance**, switching between them the way I switch local profiles today — click a profile, and the whole window (sessions, skills, tools, memory, chat) re-homes to that agent's backend, so each agent runs its tasks on its own machine while I drive them richly from the master device.

The **backend capability already exists and works** — I verified it end-to-end on v0.20.4:

- `apps/desktop/electron/connection-config.ts:474` — `profileRemoteOverride()` reads `connection.json`'s `profiles.<name> = { mode:'remote', url, authMode, token }`.
- `connection-config.ts:623` — `resolveProfileBackendRoute()` case 2 routes a profile with a remote override to its own pooled backend on that remote host.
- `connection-config.ts:526` — `/api/skills`, `/api/tools`, etc. are in `LOCAL_PRIMARY_SCOPED_ROUTES`, so those panels follow the override.
- By hand-writing `connection.json` + creating a local profile as an anchor, I can switch to my WSL agent in the profile bar and see its sessions/identity/data and chat with it.

But the **UI for this was removed**:

- `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/gateway-settings.test.tsx:47` — `// The legacy per-profile scope switcher must not render.` This switcher existed once and is now gone; the only way to configure a per-profile remote override is to hand-edit `connection.json` (`main.ts:759` — `DESKTOP_CONNECTION_CONFIG_PATH = …/connection.json`).
- The BOTS panel's remote rows are **@-mention only, not switchable**: `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js:9721` — `onOpen: bot => … bot.remoteSource ? notify("Stay in this chat and @… to message them") : switchProfile(bot.name)`. A remote agent listed in BOTS cannot be switched to, unlike a local profile.

So a very common multi-machine / cloud workflow is only reachable by hand-writing JSON, manually creating a profile anchor, and fighting name-collision pitfalls (a local profile, a v1 override key, and a v2 connection id all named the same collide — I hit this exact bug). This is not a missing capability; it is a **regression of its UI**.

## Proposed Solution

1. **Restore the per-profile remote override UI** in Settings (per profile: name, `mode: remote/cloud`, URL, token) — the same thing `connection.json` expresses, but through the UI instead of hand-edited JSON.
2. **Let BOTS remote rows switch**, not just @-mention — add a "switch to this remote profile" action to remote rows (or at least an explicit switch affordance), so a remote agent behaves as close to a local profile as possible.
3. **Don't gate the feature behind removal — add safety prompts instead.** Remote switching carries real risks (cross-machine tokens, re-homing the whole window), but "add a warning" beats "delete the feature". Suggested safeguards, all compatible with the existing machinery:
   - A one-time confirmation + risk note when configuring a remote override ("the token will be stored locally and sent to the remote host").
   - Store tokens via `safeStorage` (the existing `tokenSet`/`tokenPreview` path already does this).
   - Optional per-connection "remote" badge in the profile bar / BOTS row.
   - Keep it **opt-in** and reversible — the same spirit as the existing "never silently run in the last repo" guard, but not a blanket removal.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Hand-written `connection.json` + local profile anchor** (current) — works (I verified), but no UI, invisible to normal users, and name collisions between local profile / override key / v2 connection id are easy to trigger.
- **v2 registry remote connection (`connections.json`)** — only surfaces the agent in the BOTS panel for @-mention delivery; it does not switch the profile.
- **Local-only multi-profile** — only covers same-machine profiles; cannot cover WSL/cloud/other machines.

## Feature Type

Configuration option

## Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines) — the routing backend already exists; this is mostly restoring UI + safety prompts.

items.title: bug: DaemonThreadPoolExecutor crashes on Python 3.14+ (AttributeError)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### Describe the bug
On Python 3.14+, executing asynchronous tools or any tasks using `DaemonThreadPoolExecutor` crashes instantly with the following error:
```text
AttributeError: 'DaemonThreadPoolExecutor' object has no attribute '_initializer'
```

### To Reproduce
Run the following code on Python 3.14+:
```python
from tools.daemon_pool import DaemonThreadPoolExecutor
pool = DaemonThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2)
pool.submit(lambda: 42)
```

**Output/Traceback:**
```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
    from tools.daemon_pool import DaemonThreadPoolExecutor; pool = DaemonThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2); pool.submit(lambda: 42)
  File ".../Lib/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 215, in submit
    self._adjust_thread_count()
  File ".../tools/daemon_pool.py", line 58, in _adjust_thread_count
    self._initializer,
AttributeError: 'DaemonThreadPoolExecutor' object has no attribute '_initializer'
```

### Root Cause
In Python 3.14, `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` was refactored. The constructor no longer defines private attributes `self._initializer` or `self._initargs`. Instead, it uses `self._create_worker_context()` to initialize the worker thread context. 
Since `DaemonThreadPoolExecutor` overrides `_adjust_thread_count` to spin daemon threads, the direct access to `self._initializer` and `self._initargs` triggers an `AttributeError` on Python 3.14+, and fails to pass the correct arguments to the `_worker` target.

items.title: Codex OAuth: provider-injected prompt_cache_retention 400 aborts the turn instead of retrying

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

The Codex OAuth backend (`chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`) intermittently rejects requests with:

```
HTTP 400 - {'error': {'message': 'prompt_cache_retention is not supported on this model',
 'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'param': 'prompt_cache_retention',
 'code': 'invalid_parameter'}}
```

Hermes **never sends** `prompt_cache_retention` on this route — the provider injects it into its own upstream call and then rejects it. `agent/error_classifier.py` classifies the 400 as a deterministic `format_error` (`retryable=False`), which trips the `is_client_error` abort gate in `agent/conversation_loop.py` and kills the turn on the first attempt.

Because the request is actually fine, a plain retry succeeds ~80% of the time. Instead, the whole turn is discarded — on a large-context session that is a very expensive abort for a transient provider fault.

## Environment

- Hermes v0.20.4 (`main` @ `9162ea6db`), Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.11.15
- provider `openai-codex`, model `gpt-5.6-sol`, `api_mode: codex_responses`

## Evidence that Hermes is not the sender

`agent/transports/codex.py::_default_prompt_cache_retention_for_request` only returns a value for `api.meta.ai` and `bedrock-mantle.*.api.aws` hosts. It is never set for `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`.

Confirmed against the actual request body Hermes dumped on failure (`request_dump_*.json`) — full key list:

```
model, instructions, input, store, tools, reasoning,
include, tool_choice, parallel_tool_calls, prompt_cache_key, extra_headers
```

No `prompt_cache_retention`.

## Reproduction

A hand-built minimal request to the same endpoint, carrying **no cache parameters at all**:

```python
body = {"model": "gpt-5.6-sol", "instructions": "t",
        "input": [{"role": "user", "content": "OK"}],
        "store": False, "stream": True}
```

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| n=20 sequential | **4 failed (20%)** with this exact error |
| n=12 concurrent | 0 failed |

It is random, and it fires on requests that cannot contain the parameter.

Two distinct error shapes show where the injection happens. Deliberately sending the parameter gets the Codex gateway's own terse validator:

```json
{"detail":"Unsupported parameter: prompt_cache_retention"}
```

The spontaneous failures arrive in the OpenAI platform error envelope instead (`invalid_parameter` / `param: prompt_cache_retention`) — a different rejecter, i.e. the backend's own upstream call.

The same parameter has recently broken Azure OpenAI deployments and Cursor, consistent with a partially rolled-out feature rather than anything client-side.

## Current vs expected behaviour

```
classify_api_error(...) ->
  reason          : FailoverReason.format_error
  retryable       : False
  should_fallback : True
```

`format_error` is the correct rule for a *deterministic* bad parameter (retrying reproduces it), but wrong here: the request was valid and the failure is a coin flip. Expected: retryable, so the existing retry loop absorbs it.

## Impact

Two long-running sessions hit this 25 seconds apart, each carrying ~410-550k tokens of context. Every abort discarded a full large-context input for zero output. At a ~20% per-attempt failure rate this is not rare.

## Suggested fix

Treat a 400 that blames a parameter the current route never sends as a transient server-side fault (retryable `server_error`, `should_compress=False`), while keeping genuine client-side bad-parameter 400s (e.g. `max_tokens` on a GPT-5 model) failing fast as `format_error`. The sibling 5xx request-validation branch in `_classify_by_status` needs the same guard, since a fronting proxy can surface the identical rejection as 500/502.

PR follows.

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes already ships `/refine` (`hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py::_handle_refine_command`) which forks a background review agent that writes memory + skill updates. Those writes are currently **irrevocable** — if a review pass saves or edits something wrong, there is no built-in undo. This proposal adds a **snapshot-before-write + atomic-restore** safety net so a `/refine` run can be undone with `/refine undo`.

This is a port of prime-agent's "reversible self-improvement" feature, folded into the existing `/refine` machinery — **no architecture fork, no prompt-cache or message-role invariant break** (F1 touches only memory/skill files).

## Scope (intentionally narrow)

- New `agent/refine_rollback.py` (stdlib-only, fully unit-tested) — snapshot/restore/list/index.

items.body:
Every TUI startup prints this even though `.env` never sets `TERMINAL_CWD`:

```
⚠ Deprecated .env settings detected:
  ⚠ TERMINAL_CWD=/Users/you found in .env — this is deprecated.
```

**Root cause**

`warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` in `hermes_cli/config.py` decides ".env sets TERMINAL_CWD" from the process environment alone. But Hermes exports that variable into `os.environ` itself at runtime: `gateway/run.py:2504`, `cli.py:8473` (session restore), `cron/scheduler.py:5087` (per job), `tui_gateway/server.py:12559`, plus the worktree paths in `cli.py:20298` and `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py:1287`. So any install where `config.yaml` keeps the default `terminal.cwd: .` (which doesn't count as "explicit" in the checker) warns on every startup, with nothing to migrate. The config-to-env bridge is not the setter either; it explicitly skips `cwd: .`.

**Repro**

1. Clean `~/.hermes/.env` with no `TERMINAL_CWD` line
2. `config.yaml` with default `terminal.cwd: .` (or no terminal section)
3. Start the TUI after any code path above has run (gateway, session restore, cron)
4. Warning prints, and the suggested migration is a no-op

**Fix**

Gate the warning on what `.env` actually contains: read `HERMES_HOME/.env` and warn only when an uncommented `TERMINAL_CWD=` (or `export TERMINAL_CWD=`) line exists. Same for `MESSAGING_CWD`. Patch with a regression test is ready; PR to follow.

items.title: [Feature Request] Make per-bot Sessions open as a dockable, persistent pane
items.body:
# Feature Request: make per-bot "Sessions" open as a dockable, persistent pane

## Summary

In Hermes Desktop, the per-bot **Sessions** view (currently reached via right-click →
**Sessions** on a bot in the Bots roster) opens as a **temporary in-memory view that
replaces the roster pane**. It has no tab of its own, cannot be dragged/pinned, and
does not survive a reload — unlike the Cronjobs pane, which is a docked, persistent pane.

This request is to make the per-bot Sessions view a real, **dockable + persistent pane**
(like Cronjobs), so a user can pin it in the layout and keep it open across sessions.

## Why it matters

- The general sidebar **Sessions** pane already exists and is dockable — but it does
  **not filter by individual bot**. To inspect one bot's sessions you must use the
  right-click → Sessions action, which gives a floating, non-persistent view.
- For users managing several bots (multi-profile fleets), being able to **pin a
  bot's sessions panel** next to the chat (same as pinning Cronjobs) is a natural
  workflow need.

## Current behavior (from the code)

In `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js`:

- Right-click → Sessions calls `openBotSessionsWorkspace(bot)`, which sets an
  in-memory atom `$botSessionsWorkspace` (`const $botSessionsWorkspace = atom(null)`,
  line ~186).
- When set, `BotsPane` returns `ProfileSessionsWorkspace` (line ~9357–9358) instead
  of the roster — i.e. it **replaces the roster content** rather than opening a pane.
- The atom is **not persisted** (no `localStorage`/`paneStates.v1` entry), so the view
  is lost on reload / bot switch.

## Proposed change

1. Register a new contributed pane (e.g. `BotSessions`) using the same pane/dock
   mechanism the plugin already uses for **Bots** (`data.dock`, e.g.
   `dock: { pane: 'sessions', pos: 'center', enforce: true }`, line ~9890–9913).
2. Render the existing `ProfileSessionsWorkspace` inside that pane instead of inside
   the roster, keeping the roster intact when the pane is open.
3. Persist the pane's open state (and which bot it shows) through the existing
   `paneStates.v1` localStorage mechanism so it survives reloads, matching Cronjobs.

## Acceptance criteria

- Right-click → Sessions opens a **dockable pane** (draggable / pinnable) rather than
  replacing the roster.
- The pane state (open/bot/tab placement) **persists** across app reloads.
- Opening the Sessions pane does **not** hide or reset the Bots roster.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop (apps/desktop), packaged build.
- Seen on current version; unrelated to any auth/gateway state.

items.body:
# Gateway self-heal wedges after Telegram polling network outage (2026-08-20)

**Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)** | Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0.0-28) | Python 3.12.3
Messaging: telegram (polling mode, direct connection, DoH-discovered fallback IP) + weixin
Deployment: `systemd --user` service `hermes-gateway.service` (Restart=always)

## Summary

After a Telegram long-polling network outage, the gateway's retryable-fatal error path
**wedges the main loop**. The adapter correctly marks the platform retryable-fatal after
10 failed reconnect attempts, but the supervisor handler (`_handle_adapter_fatal_error`)
logs the ERROR line and then **never proceeds** — the expected
`queued for background reconnection` / `gateway staying alive, watcher will retry`
log lines never appear, and the background reconnect watcher never takes over.
Telegram stayed disconnected for **4h17m** until a manual process re-start. The cron
scheduler (separate asyncio task) kept running normally the whole time; only the
messaging main loop was wedged.

## Timeline (all times CST, UTC+8)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| ~03:50 | Telegram long-poll connection reset (empty error, CLOSE-WAIT socket seen at 03:50:21) — typical network-path reset on direct connection |
| 03:50:01 -> 04:02:31 | 10 exponential-backoff retries (5s->60s cap), all failed, error text empty |
| 04:02:31,296 | adapter: `Telegram polling could not reconnect after 10 network error retries.` (logs "Restarting gateway.") |
| 04:02:31,302 | gateway.run: `Fatal telegram adapter error (telegram_network_error): ...` |
| 04:02:31 -> 08:07 | **COMPLETE LOG SILENCE** in both `gateway.log` and journald — no housekeeping, no reconnect attempts, no watcher activity. Cron jobs (agent.log) ran every 2 min uninterrupted. |
| 07:00:45 | a cron job's `send_message` to Telegram **succeeded** (only a MarkdownV2 parse warning) -> network was back by 07:00, but the polling connection was never re-established (send-only, no receive) |
| 08:07 | manual `systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway` -> Telegram connected in 2s, everything recovered |

## Evidence (key log lines)

```
2026-08-20 03:50:01,269 WARNING ...: [Telegram] Telegram polling degraded (heartbeat probe); gateway stays alive and will retry. Error:
2026-08-20 03:50:21,272 WARNING ...: [Telegram] updater.stop() timed out during network-error reconnect (likely CLOSE-WAIT socket); forcing drain and restart without clean stop
2026-08-20 04:02:31,296 ERROR ...: [Telegram] Telegram polling could not reconnect after 10 network error retries. Restarting gateway. Last error:
2026-08-20 04:02:31,302 ERROR gateway.run: Fatal telegram adapter error (telegram_network_error): Telegram polling could not reconnect after 10 network error retries. Restarting gateway.
```
After the last ERROR line: nothing for 4h17m. PID stayed constant (207480); process
alive, event loop alive (cron ran), but the gateway main loop produced no logging and
performed no recovery.

## Root-cause analysis

Code path: `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:2360` (`_polling_network_error_count > MAX_NETWORK_RETRIES`
-> `_set_fatal_error(..., retryable=True)` + `_notify_fatal_error()`) ->
`gateway/run.py:4325` `_handle_adapter_fatal_error()`.

Expected sequence in `_handle_adapter_fatal_error`:
1. log ERROR (happened)
2. `_update_platform_runtime_status(...)` (unknown — no subsequent logs)
3. `await self._safe_adapter_disconnect(...)` (bounded by `_adapter_disconnect_timeout_secs`, ~210s default)
4. queue platform into `_failed_platforms` + log `queued for background reconnection`
5. log `gateway staying alive, watcher will retry in background`

Observed: only step 1 produced output. Steps 2-5's log lines are absent from both
`gateway.log` and journald for 4h17m. The reconnect watcher therefore never ran.
`_safe_adapter_disconnect` is timeout-bounded, so the wedge is likely either in
`_update_platform_runtime_status` (status file write path) or in an await that swallows
CancelledError despite the `_await_adapter_cleanup_with_timeout` mitigation
(e.g. `adapter.disconnect()` never yielding past the watchdog's cancel, with
`consume_detached_task_result` keeping no visible trace). Notably, `errors.log` shows
`updater.stop() timed out` (CLOSE-WAIT) earlier in the same outage, suggesting the
python-telegram-bot teardown path was already wedged before the fatal handler ran.

## Impact

- Telegram channel down ~4h17m (03:50 -> 08:07), only recoverable by manual process re-start.
- All other gateway functions (cron scheduler, weixin send path, agent runs) unaffected.
- This is the second failure mode of the same outage: the "keep gateway alive, reconnect
  in background" design (introduced to avoid re-start loops) failed to actually reconnect.

## Suggested investigation

1. Reproduce: simulate 10 consecutive Telegram network errors with a wedged socket and
   observe whether `_handle_adapter_fatal_error` reaches step 4.
2. Audit awaits between the ERROR log and the `_failed_platforms` enqueue for unbounded
   or cancellation-swallowing paths (especially `adapter.disconnect()` and the runtime
   status write).
3. Consider adding a watchdog on the platform-state file (`gateway_state.json`): if
   `telegram.state` stays non-connected for N minutes, force a hard re-start.

## Local mitigation (user side)

A cron watchdog (`~/.hermes/scripts/gateway_watchdog.py`, every 5 min) now re-starts the
gateway if `gateway_state.json` shows fatal/retrying/disconnected, or if `connected` has
not refreshed in 15 min — with a 10-min re-start cooldown to avoid re-start storms.

---

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
Summary
Updating Hermes from the Desktop app on Windows can hang indefinitely at the "Updating Hermes" screen when a WeChat/Feishu gateway is configured to stay resident. The update pipeline itself completes (git pull, deps, rebuild), but the background hand-off script never finishes, so the result file is never written, the .hermes-update-in-progress marker is never cleared, and the Desktop stays on "Updating Hermes" until manually recovered.
Environment
- Hermes Agent 40.10.2, upstream main ad889540f
- Windows 11, git install, Desktop app (Electron)
- Weixin platform configured; gateway kept resident (this is the trigger)
Root cause
scripts/desktop-update/windows.ps1 — Invoke-HermesStep starts the updater with RedirectStandardOutput/RedirectStandardError and waits via:
$outTask = $proc.StandardOutput.ReadToEndAsync()
$errTask = $proc.StandardError.ReadToEndAsync()
...
$proc.WaitForExit()
...
$outTask.Result   # never returns
The updater is invoked as hermes update --yes --gateway --force --branch main. On the last step the updater spawns the resident gateway (gateway run --replace). The gateway inherits the updater's stdout/stderr pipe handles, so the pipe never reaches EOF, ReadToEndAsync never completes, and the hand-off script blocks forever on .Result. The hand-off then never writes .hermes-update-result.json, never removes .hermes-update-in-progress, and never relaunches the Desktop.
Confirmed by inspecting scripts/desktop-update/windows.ps1 in main at ad889540f.
Log evidence
- logs/desktop-update-handoff.log stops after the step banner with no exit code line, while the updater itself had already completed (Hermes.exe rebuilt, desktop-build-stamp updated).
- Killing the gateway immediately unblocks the script; the script then finishes the hand-off cleanly.
- After manual recovery, logs/desktop.log shows detached update finished OK (branch main) and the gateway reconnects ([Weixin] Connected).
Suggested fixes
1. Detach the gateway so it does not inherit the updater's pipes. Launch it with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP/a separate job object, or otherwise close/repoint the inherited stdout/stderr handles so the parent pipe can reach EOF (e.g. redirect to NUL before spawning the resident child).
2. Don't block the hand-off on the updater's live descendant. In windows.ps1, avoid $proc.StandardOutput.ReadToEndAsync().Result as an EOF wait; use an explicit timeout plus WaitForExit, or spawn the updater with a detached console.
3. Stale-marker watchdog. If the hand-off script or updater makes no progress for > N minutes, write a failed result and clear .hermes-update-in-progress, so the Desktop never shows a dead-end "Updating Hermes" screen.
Related
Similar symptom family but different root cause: #87772 (stale marker after hung cua-driver installer). #90205 fixed a different hand-off hang (stdin treated as tty → "Restore local changes?" prompt) and is already in main; it does not address this pipe-EOF deadlock.
